header:
Date: 2026-12-07 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM); Maria Lopez (Crestline Procurement), Samir Patel (Crestline Infosec), Ellen Wright (Crestline Legal), Tom Rivers (Crestline ML)
summary: Procurement and legal kickoff to review Redwood MSA/DPA, discuss SLA targets and pricing approval path. Crestline emphasized data residency and KMS/HSM requirements; security team requested SOC2 artifacts and audit log details. Next steps: Redwood to send contractual documents and SLA matrix; SE to run benchmarks and CSM to coordinate onboarding timeline.
topics: SLA targets: uptime and latency SLOs + credits
Pricing approval path and billing cadence
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Cole: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We have about 50 minutes, lots to cover MSA and DPA and then Jordan will take the technical bench... um the benchmark plan.
[00:08] Maria Lopez: Hi Avery, thanks. We invited legal and security because procurement needs to get the MSA and DPA locked, and we need to understand SLAs before we can move to PO.
[00:16] Ellen Wright: Yeah hi, quick overview from legal, we'll be focused on indemnity, data handling, and the DPA. We'll have a redline doc but want to surface any non-starters early.
[00:25] Jordan Kim: Great, I'll save most technical detail for later — but quick note, Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private VPC deploys, and there's a consistent API layer. For pilot we typically recommend hosted dedicated burst config or private depending on data residency.
[00:37] Samir Patel: On security side we need SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 if you have it, SSO SAML integration details, KMS/HSM key management, and audit log retention. Also how you handle tenant isolation on dedicated.
[00:49] Priya Desai: We'll share the links to our compliance pack, but note that for private deployments we can support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
[00:58] Tom Rivers: From engineering, we're primarily concerned about latency SLOs if we hit 200 QPS and also about KV cache behavior and warm start latencies.
[01:10] Avery Cole: Understood — on SLAs we usually offer 99.9% uptime for hosted with credits, and higher options for Dedicated. For latency we have documented percentiles per model in the SLA matrix which I'll share. We're flexible — if you need 99.95 we can discuss dedicated or higher-tier capacity.
[01:28] Maria Lopez: Procurement needs concrete numbers to get internal approvals. Can you confirm escalation to legal and the timeline for signed MSA? We have an internal board review next week.
[01:36] Avery Cole: We'll aim to get the standard MSA and DPA over by Thursday, 2026-12-10. Ellen, that should give you time to redline ahead of your review?
[01:44] Ellen Wright: Thursday is workable. We'll try to return redlines within a week but need to coordinate with procurement on pricing clauses.
[01:51] Jordan Kim: Technical note — for the pilot we suggest three models: a smaller quantized model for embedding workloads, a mid-size for chat, and a larger for high-quality transforms. We'll include expected p95/p99 latencies per model on A100 and on our CPU fallback.
[02:08] Samir Patel: Can Redwood support HSM-backed keys? We require hardware key separation for production PII.
[02:14] Priya Desai: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS and HSM options; we'll detail key rotation and access controls in the compliance pack.
[02:22] Tom Rivers: Also need clarification on data residency — some of our data must remain in EU regions. Do you have regional hosting guarantees?
[02:29] Avery Cole: Yes, we have region routing policies and can pin workloads to a region or private deployment — we'll note region options in the SLA matrix.
[02:36] Maria Lopez: About pricing — procurement needs the pricing sheet with committed usage tiers and overage rules. We typically need a 12-month commitment model to get sign-off.
[02:45] Avery Cole: We'll include both pay-as-you-go and reserved capacity pricing in the spreadsheet. Reserved (Dedicated) gives better unit economics and SLA.
[02:52] Ellen Wright: On indemnity we have a few standard clauses we'll likely ask to modify; specifically limitation of liability caps and data breach notification timelines. We also need to confirm breach notification timing — 72 hours?
[03:02] Avery Cole: Standard is 72 hours for incidents; we can confirm in the DPA. For liability caps, our legal team typically proposes mutual caps, but we'll await your redline.
[03:11] [03:15] Jordan Kim: Moving to the technical deep dive — I'll share screen in a follow-up demo but to set expectations: benchmarking will include cold start, steady-state throughput, and prefix caching performance. We do KV cache on a per-session basis and automatic prefix caching can save tok- costs.
[03:29] Tom Rivers: When you say KV cache can you clarify persistent cache across requests or just in-memory per instance? We've seen inconsistent documentation where folks say KV cache but it's ephemeral.
[03:38] Jordan Kim: Good point — it's primarily in-memory but we can persist prefix caches for dedicated/private deployments; I'll put exact behavior in the benchmark doc. Apologies if earlier materials were unclear — sometimes the auto transcript calls it K V cash or K V cache, sorry.
[03:53] Samir Patel: Can we talk about audit logs and retention? We need immutable logs for 7 years for some regs. Is that possible?
[04:00] Priya Desai: We offer configurable retention windows for audit logs in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have standard retention but can work with enterprise add-ons.
[04:09] Maria Lopez: On billing cadence, we prefer monthly with a 30-day net. Does Redwood accept ACH and wire? Any vendor onboarding paperwork needed?
[04:18] Avery Cole: We accept ACH/wire; we'll send vendor forms and W-9. Payment terms can be aligned to your procurement policy; monthly billing is standard, and reserved contracts can be annual with monthly invoices too.
[04:29] Ellen Wright: A few practical asks — please label any data exfil controls clearly and confirm whether log data contains PII or is redacted. We need to know for the DPA.
[04:38] Jordan Kim: By default logs are metadata and request traces; we can configure redaction and token-level controls. For model outputs we recommend customers not send raw PII, but if required we provide encryption at rest and in transit and KMS options.
[04:50] [05:05] Maria Lopez: Timeline question: if we get the MSA signed by mid-December, what is realistic for pilot start? We need integration in our staging and a security review.
[05:13] Priya Desai: For a standard pilot onboarding we typically need 2-3 weeks for provisioning and benchmarking, longer for private installs. If MSA is signed mid-December, early January pilot start is realistic.
[05:24] Tom Rivers: For the pilot we'll need a list of required network ports and a small infra checklist. Also can you provide a runbook for incident response?
[05:32] Jordan Kim: Yes — we will include network diagrams, required ports, and incident runbook.
[05:38] Maria Lopez: Procurement will also ask about SLAs tied to credits. Can you spell out the credits formula?
[05:44] Avery Cole: SLA credits are percent-of-monthly-invoice based for downtime windows. For example, for hosted 99.9% you get 10% credit for the month if below threshold, piecewise scales. For Dedicated higher SLOs we can negotiate steeper remedies or service credits. We'll provide the exact matrix.
[05:59] Ellen Wright: One other thing — data deletion on contract termination. We need assurance of secure deletion and certification.
[06:06] Priya Desai: We offer data deletion certificates for enterprise engagements; we'll document the process and retention timelines in the DPA.
[06:14] Tom Rivers: Benchmarks — Jordan, can you propose a minimal dataset for perf tests? We prefer synthetic data to avoid shipping PII to third parties.
[06:21] Jordan Kim: Absolutely, synthetic is preferred; we'll propose a representative synthetic trace and metrics to measure p50/p95/p99 and token costs.
[06:29] Samir Patel: Regarding network access, do you require inbound peering or can you do VPC egress-only? For private installs we need strict egress controls.
[06:36] Jordan Kim: Private can be done with customer-managed VPC peering and egress-only options; we'll include networking options in the onboarding doc.
[06:44] Maria Lopez: Circling back to pricing sign-off — our finance owner requires a 12-month committed baseline and a break clause after 90 days if SLAs are not met. Is that typical?
[06:53] Avery Cole: We can accommodate trial clauses and SLA-based termination windows in enterprise contracts — that's negotiable. I will flag that for the legal team.
[07:01] [07:20] Jordan Kim: Quick note on model variants — we can route to cheaper quantized variants automatically if latency tolerance is higher; that helps cost control. We can also set weights for canary rollouts.
[07:31] Tom Rivers: Can you share an example dashboard view of cost/latency per token? Our platform team needs visibility.
[07:38] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll share sample screenshots and a short screencast.
[07:48] Samir Patel: About encryption — in transit TLS 1.2+ and at rest AES-256? Any FIPS mode?
[07:55] Jordan Kim: TLS 1.2/1.3 supported, AES-256 at rest, FIPS/HSM options available for private/dedicated with partner HSMs. We'll detail that.
[08:03] Maria Lopez: Procurement might ask for references from other energy customers or similar regulated industries. Do you have any references?
[08:09] Avery Cole: We can share redacted references and case studies from regulated customers; I'll include one or two relevant references.
[08:16] Ellen Wright: For contract language, please note our standard data breach notification clause and a 72-hour window; we may propose additional audits on-site if needed.
[08:24] Priya Desai: On-site audits are possible for Private deployments; for hosted we provide audit artifacts and SOC2.
[08:30] [08:45] Jordan Kim: Technical clarifier — when you asked earlier about cache persistence, for hosted ephemeral is default, for dedicated we can persist prefix cache or use a shared cache with customer-managed backing for low-latency repeated contexts.
[08:58] Tom Rivers: That's helpful. Also need explanation of graceful degradation — how you fallback when capacity is constrained.
[09:06] Jordan Kim: Smart routing will fall back to compatible model variants or alternate region, and there are automatic degradation policies we can configure per route.
[09:13] Maria Lopez: Can you add the SLA for failover time? Our app requires sub-second or low single-digit second failover for routing.
[09:21] Avery Cole: We'll include failover and routing policy details and measurable SLOs.
[09:27] Ellen Wright: Is there a standard escrow for IP or source in case of company failure? Procurement asks about continuity.
[09:34] Avery Cole: We don't typically escrow model binaries; we provide migration guides and data export. We can discuss bespoke continuity arrangements for enterprise.
[09:42] [09:55] Maria Lopez: Any minimum security questionnaire we need to fill? We often have an RFP security questionnaire.
[10:00] Priya Desai: We can provide an ATO security questionnaire or a standard vendor security form. Send your questionnaire and we'll return it completed.
[10:08] Tom Rivers: For the benchmark SLA, can Redwood provide baseline p95 latencies with 95% confidence intervals?
[10:15] Jordan Kim: Yes, we'll include statistical measures in the benchmark plan.
[10:20] Maria Lopez: Great. What about proof of insurance and cyber liability? That's another procurement requirement.
[10:26] Avery Cole: We will attach certificates of insurance; we'll get them to you via the vendor onboarding packet.
[10:33] [10:50] Ellen Wright: Regarding DPA, please confirm data processor subprocessors list and the right to audit subprocessors.
[10:58] Priya Desai: We'll include subprocessors list and standard audit rights; for private deployments subprocessors are limited.
[11:06] Samir Patel: Also need API-level auth details: per-token RBAC, rotation windows, and secrets management.
[11:13] Jordan Kim: We support per-api-key RBAC, rotation policies, and integrate with vaults/KMS. We'll include examples.
[11:20] Maria Lopez: Procurement will want a single point of contact for billing and legal. Can we consolidate?
[11:25] Avery Cole: Yes — I'll be primary contact for procurement and I'll loop Priya for onboarding and Jordan for tech.
[11:33] Ellen Wright: If you could put all docs in a shared folder and invite legal, that would expedite the review.
[11:40] Avery Cole: We'll create a shared drive link and send it in the follow-up email.
[11:48] [12:00] Jordan Kim: On pilot metrics we'll measure latency, throughput, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll deliver results and a recommended config.
[12:09] Tom Rivers: For the price sheet, include reserved pricing for 6 and 12 month commits. We'll evaluate the 12-month.
[12:16] Maria Lopez: Also include termination for convenience clause and exit assistance.
[12:22] Avery Cole: We'll include exit assistance and data export/secure deletion terms.
[12:29] Priya Desai: For onboarding timeline — typical steps: paperwork, security review, provisioning, bench- marking, pilot, then production rollout. We'll map tasks and owners.
[12:38] Maria Lopez: Any standard onboarding SLA for Redwood to provision accounts?
[12:45] Priya Desai: For hosted we typically provision within 3 business days after contract; dedicated and private have longer lead times.
[12:54] [13:10] Ellen Wright: Logistically we'll review the MSA/DPA, the team will propose redlines and we aim to have legal signoff by 2026-12-17 if possible.
[13:20] Avery Cole: Great. We'll follow up with the MSA/DPA and the SLA/pricing spreadsheet. Any final open questions?
[13:28] Tom Rivers: One micro question — model explainability and provenance: do you provide model metadata and versioning so we can track regressions?
[13:36] Jordan Kim: Yes — model catalog includes versioning, inference profiles, and rollout history. We'll include provenance docs.
[13:45] Maria Lopez: That's it from procurement for now. Thanks everyone.
[13:50] Avery Cole: Thanks all. Recap: send docs by Thursday, Jordan will plan benchmarks, Ellen to redline, Samir to send security checklist. We'll reconvene after initial redlines.
[14:02] Ellen Wright: Sounds good.
[14:05] Samir Patel: Thank you.
[14:07] Priya Desai: Thanks all — will send calendar hold for follow-up.
[14:10] Avery Cole: End call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (KV cache heard as K V cash), speaker overlap at times, some timestamps approximate. The call lasted 52 minutes; timestamp indices above are conversational markers not full minute-by-minute log.
